questions.question: A CMV should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher unless carrying hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher unless traveling through remote areas.
Not have a fire extinguisher.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is properly charged and rated.

questions.question: When stopped at a railroad crossing, a bus driver can hear an approaching train by:

options.text: Opening the emergency window.
Opening the front door.
Waiting for passengers to be quiet on their own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the front door.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, buses must stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. The driver should look both ways for trains. Open the front door if it helps you see or hear a train coming.

questions.question: Do not base your gear shift decision on:

options.text: Your engine speed (rpm).
Your vehicle speed (mph).
What the vehicle next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speedometer. Learn which speeds work best for each gear. Never shift based on other vehicles' actions.

questions.question: Check your mirrors:

options.text: Before every lane change.
When changing lanes only if other vehicles are nearby.
When changing lanes only when it is dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every lane change.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors before changing lanes. Make mirror checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, you should:

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Not use your mirrors to check other lanes.
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid a crash, always keep both hands on the wheel. A firm grip lets you turn quickly and stay in control.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Front tires need a tread depth of at least 4/32 inch.
Tires should be slightly deflated.
Rear tires need a tread depth of at least 2/32 inch.
Use a gauge to check tire tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires should be slightly deflated.
questions.explanation: In winter, tires need good tread to grip the road. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch and rear tires need at least 2/32 inch. Use a gauge to check tread. Do not deflate tires—this reduces traction.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on the vehicle.
Face the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When exiting during the vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic test failure.

questions.question: For a standard parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull directly into the space without passing it first.
Back directly into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your right. Then back into it, bringing your vehicle's rear end as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is using high beam lights, you should:

options.text: Look directly at the headlights.
Flash your high beams to signal the driver.
Look to the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
Pull to the side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle comes toward you with high beams on, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road. This prevents the bright lights from blinding you.

questions.question: When driving in fog, the safest action is to:

options.text: Stay in the left lane.
Avoid driving in fog.
Use your low beam lights.
Follow the vehicle ahead closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving in fog.
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see the road, other vehicles, and hazards. Do not drive in fog if possible.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which is not a problem?

options.text: Loose or broken exhaust pipes
Loose or broken mounting brackets
Leaking exhaust system parts
Exhaust system parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts
questions.explanation: Check the exhaust system for these problems: loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, or stacks; loose, broken, or missing brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts; exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other vehicle parts; and leaking exhaust parts.

questions.question: Your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: Exactly where the examiner instructed.
Within five feet of the position the examiner described.
Wherever you can safely park.
Within two feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner instructed.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact position the examiner told you to use. If you do not complete an exercise exactly as the examiner described, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: After picking up passengers at a stop, a driver should:

options.text: Give passengers time to sit or hold on before starting to drive.
Honk the horn and enter traffic right away.
Start driving as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give passengers time to sit or hold on before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Start and stop smoothly to keep passengers safe. After passengers board, wait for them to sit down or get a good grip before you drive.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact.
Try to block their way.
Ignore any hand gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore any hand gestures.
questions.explanation: The best thing to do with an aggressive driver is to get out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact, as this may anger them. Ignore any gestures they make.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, which should you not do?

options.text: Move your vehicle to the side of the road
Help any injured people
Drive away from the scene

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive away from the scene
questions.explanation: In an accident, protect the area, call authorities, help the injured, get information from others, and report the accident. Leaving the scene can cause you to lose your license.

questions.question: An example of required emergency equipment is:

options.text: A supply of spare electrical fuses.
A loud horn.
A battery-operated flashlight.
A supply of fireworks.

questions.correctAnswerText: A supply of spare electrical fuses.
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher; spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers); and warning devices for parked vehicles, such as reflective triangles.

questions.question: A smaller vehicle than yours will usually:

options.text: Stop faster than your vehicle.
Take longer to stop than your vehicle.
Take about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can stop faster than larger vehicles. Keep this in mind when deciding how far back to stay from other cars.

questions.question: Regrooved tires are:

options.text: Allowed only on the front of a bus.
Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus.

questions.question: Reaching unsafely for a phone while driving is:

options.text: Okay if you are driving alone.
Okay if you will use a hands-free feature.
Never okay, even with a hands-free feature.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never okay, even with a hands-free feature.
questions.explanation: Your phone must be within easy reach and close to you while you are safely seated and buckled in. It is dangerous and not allowed to reach unsafely for your phone, even if you plan to use a hands-free feature.

questions.question: If a tire fails while driving, you should:

options.text: Brake as hard as possible.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Avoid braking and let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Stop on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid braking and let the vehicle slow down on its own.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, hold the steering wheel firmly. Do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down by itself. Once it slows down a lot, brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.
